label: Catholic Church, Catechism of the Catholic…: CCC 36-38: the Catechism teaches, quoting Dei Filius…
locator: CCC 36-38, Our holy mother, the Church, holds and teaches that God ... can be known with certainty from the created world by the natural light of human reason
interpretation: CCC 36 quotes Dei Filius ch. 2 (DS 3004); CCC 37-38 add the difficulties of knowing God 'by the light of reason alone' in historical conditions (Humani generis) and the need of revelation so that these truths 'can be known by all men with ease, with firm certainty and with no admixture of error'. Read in the official English translation. It states what the Catechism teaches, not what believers in fact affirm.
attribution: The passage states that the Catechism, quoting Dei Filius, teaches that God can be known with certainty from the created world by the natural light of human reason, and that it adds the historical difficulties of doing so, which is the premise.
